name: Molybdenum
occurrence: Mined mainly from molybdenite ore, often as a by-product of copper mining.
majorUses: High-strength steel alloys (drill bits, armour plating)
Electrical contacts and furnace heating elements
biologicalRelevance: An essential trace cofactor for enzymes like nitrogenase, which bacteria use to fix atmospheric nitrogen into forms plants can use — making it indirectly essential to the entire nitrogen cycle.
notableCharacteristics: Has one of the highest melting points of any element, exceeded by only a handful of metals like tungsten and rhenium.
whyHere: Like chromium above it, molybdenum's electron configuration favours a half-filled 4d⁵ 5s¹ arrangement for extra stability, and its strong metallic bonding is exactly why it survives extreme heat in alloys and furnace parts.
didYouKnow: Molybdenum is the metal at the heart of nitrogenase, the enzyme certain soil bacteria use to break nitrogen's famously tough triple bond — without it, biological nitrogen fixation as we know it wouldn't happen.
genZNote: The literal reason bacteria can fix nitrogen from air. No molybdenum, no nitrogen cycle, no you.
